paper_metadata.title: Special Features of the Structure and Phase Composition of High-Rhenium Nickel Refractory Alloy

evidence.quote: The most refractory materials produced today in Russia and in foreign countries for single crystal gas turbine blades are nickel alloys with rhenium additives [1].

We studied single crystals of refractory nickel alloy VZhM-1, the chemical composition of which is presented in Table 3. VZhM-1 belongs to high-rhenium refractory nickel alloys of the third generation and is used for casting single crystal gas turbine blades [1].
We fabricated2 single crystals from alloy VZhM-1 for study by the method of liquid metal cooling (LMC) on refectory seeds in a UVNK-9A industrial furnace for directed crystallization.
the crystals were subjected to heat treatment that included long-term (up to 26 h) many-stage homogenizing at 1285 – 1335°C and two-stage aging.

An x-ray diffraction analysis of the isolate obtained by the method of PPA has down that the crystal structure of this phase is close to the structural type of a Co 7W6 intermetallic compound (/c109-phase).

By the data of the x-ray diffraction analysis the isolated lamellar phase has an fcc lattice (structure type A1) with a constant of 0.361 nm, whereas the constants of the lattices of the /c103/c162- and /c103-phases are 0.358 – 0.359 nm. We will denote this phase /c103c . The content of rhenium in the phase (data of MXRSA)3 attains up to 30 at.%.

It can be seen from Fig. 4 that the lamellas of the /c103c-phase acquire a woven structure after long-term high-tem-perature tests, which is a consequence of spinodal decompo-sition or stratification of this phase into two other phases with ordered (L1 2 ) and disordered (A1) structures, i.e., /c103c /c174~/c162/c103+ ~/c103.

mechanisms.name: ascending diffusion of Re, W and Mo

evidence.quote: The mechanism of formation of lamellas of /c103c-phase during long-term action of high temperature seems to be connected with ascending diffusion of Re, W, and Mo atoms due to the high energy of interatomic homeopolar bonding and localization of the atoms over planes {111} of the fcc lattice of the nickel solid solution.

Rhenium, which is primarily dissolved in the nickel fcc-solid solution (/c103-phase), hinders the diffusion processes in the solution and thus increases the creep resistance of the alloy under the ac-tion of high temperatures and stresses.

It can be as-sumed that the woven structure of the /c103c-phase, which en-sures formation of new interfaces in the structure of the alloy, is an act of adaptation of the system to the rigid conditions of the tests of the single crystal specimen. This promotes de-crease in the internal stresses, hinders the processes of frac-ture of the single crystal alloy

mechanisms.name: coarsening and degradation of gamma-prime particles

evidence.quote: we found out that the decrease in the time before failure at 900 – 1100°C in the single crystals annealed at 1000°C for 500 h was caused by coarsening and degradation of particles of the main hardening /c103/c162-phase.
It is assumed [4, 5] that lamella of such quite brittle tcp-phases are stress concentrators and sources of nucleation and propagation of cracks.

conflicts.description: The source mentions reports that the main factor reducing creep resistance after long-term exposure is the unfavorable shape and size of gamma-prime particles rather than lamellar phase segregation, which contradicts the known opinion on the embrittling action of tcp-phases.

evidence.quote: The authors of [3] show that the main factor influencing the decrease in the creep resistance of the alloy after such exposures is the unfa-vorable shape and size of the particles of the /c103/c162-phase rather than the segregation of a lamellar phase, which is identified by them and a /c115-phase. This statement contradicts the known opinion on the embrittling action of tcp-phases.
